message.content: Yes, it is broadly sensible, though a bit generic for text-to-image systems. For text-to-image models, “zero-shot generalization” can reasonably mean the model can produce images for prompts involving concepts, attributes, or combinations it did not see explicitly during training, without extra fine-tuning or test-time adaptation. The main caveat is that “new unseen concepts” can be vague, since many text-to-image models are trained on broad image–caption data and may have seen related concepts even if not the exact prompt. People like Emma, Liam, and Sophia might reasonably interpret the definition as capturing the core idea: the model applies what it learned to novel prompt concepts rather than memorized examples.
